acceptanceCriteria: A failure counts as known only if it failed in the full run and the isolated re-run, and its evidence is re-read at diff time; missing or passing evidence un-excuses it.
Full-run-only failures are listed as suspected flakes and never excused.
Tests in --own files fail the gate even if known.
The receipt lists new, known, fixed and flaky sets with counts and is bound to the baseline revision.
A baseline older than a configurable bound relative to the branch point is reported as stale.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1033 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem A directory or suite run on an integration branch fails for tests that were already failing before the change. Authors are refused for failures they did not cause, or the failures are excused in prose. Current workaround Each failure is compared with an old full-run baseline. When the baseline predates the branch, a separate known-failures list is kept: the failing tests are re-run in isolation, and only those failing in both runs are listed. Failures seen only in the full run are reported as load or order flakes and never excused. Entries stay valid only while their cited run still shows the failure. Tests in the change's own files must pass outright. Proposal `corvint tests baseline record --rev REV` runs the suite, re-runs failures in isolation and stores the both-fail set with evidence run ids. `corvint tests baseline diff RUN... --own PATH...` exits non-zero on any new failu See beamfall/corvint#1033 for the full text.
title: run gate: block only on failures not in a revision-pinned baseline, with evidence-backed known-failure entries (issue #1033)
